# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

</system-reminder>

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

</system-reminder>

252	### 1. Frame update path
253	
254	One rendered frame. The tick is driven from `_process`, never from the physics callback (kernel CR-1a; see Open Question OQ-1 for three GDDs that still cite the physics callback).
255	
256	```
257	Engine frame (_process order by process_priority)
258	│
259	├─ INPUT_ADAPTER (-100)  Input Adapter (INPUT_SURFACE; the only presentation-side node below the driver's priority, so the KRN-LAT-02 priority lint exempts INPUT_SURFACE nodes)
260	│     read InputMap actions → change-only intents (set_move_intent, set_aim ≤ every 3 ticks)
261	│     → kernel.submit(type, payload, actor, correlation)            [sync call, queued]
262	│
263	├─ TICK_DRIVER (-50)  KernelHost → TickDriver (the only wall-clock read that reaches the sim)
264	│     boundary service first (SAVING / LOADING / pause / resume; a frame that ends in a transition into RUNNING clears the accumulator and discards its own delta)
265	│     then, while RUNNING: acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE ; ticks = min(floor(acc / 1e6), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME=4)
266	│     repeat ticks times: Kernel.step()  ──► P0 Begin
267	│                                           P1 Intake   (queue → this tick's batch, coalesce intents)
268	│                                           P2 Dispatch (authority check → validate → apply in WriteScope)
269	│                                           P3 Step     (hooks whose T mod divisor == offset, topo order)
270	│                                           P4 Commit
271	│                                           P5 Notify   (batches queued; PRESENTATION merged per frame)
272	│                                           P6 Boundary (snapshot/restore/pause requests)
273	│     drop lag (LAG_FORGIVE_TICKS 0) ; flush results ; compute tick_alpha
274	│
275	└─ priority 2  Presentation subscribers (render callback)
276	      handlers only mark dirty → draw using read views at tick_alpha:
277	      pos = floor(prev + (curr - prev) × tick_alpha)
278	      Avatar Presenter → Lighting → Trail → Instruments (perceived()) → HUD (perceived()) → Audio
279	      Pipeline root: CameraSolver → canvas_transform in frame_pre_draw
280	```
281	
282	**P3 hook schedule (MVP).** Divisor and offset decide which ticks a hook runs on; `after:` orders hooks that run on the same tick. An `after:` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick should declare `tolerates_stale` (CR-3); an undeclared one boots with a warning (ruling R-8), so the warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run.
283	
284	| Hook | Owner | Divisor | Offset | After |
285	|---|---|---|---|---|
286	| `controller.step` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `suit.vitals` (stale-tolerant) |
287	| `layout.doors` | Layout | 1 | 0 | — |
288	| `body.integrate` | Body | 1 | 0 | `controller.step`, `layout.doors` |
289	| `controller.noise` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate` |
290	| `emitter.place` | Emitter | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` (stale-tolerant) |
291	| `interaction.step` | Interaction | 1 | 0 | `emitter.place` |

293	| `transit.step` | Web Map | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` (**undeclared** stale edge, IC-11) |

302	The kernel builds this order once in BOOTING; an unknown `after:` id or a cycle fails boot. ADR-0003 records the sort; each owning GDD remains the authority on its own row.
303	
304	**Budgets (P99, release export, RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK):** P3 ≤ 2.0 ms (alarm at `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 ms); frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms for one tick and ≤ 6.0 ms for four; Graph hooks ≤ 0.5 ms on a hook tick; `emitter.place` + exposure ≤ 0.4 ms; Sanity median ≤ 0.5 ms; pipeline `_process` ≤ 0.5 ms; light CPU ≤ 1.0 ms steady; total frame ≤ 14.9 ms desktop and ≤ 30.0 ms Deck (90 % of the 16.6 / 33.3 ms ceilings, ruling R12).

306	### 2. Command path (a player verb)
307	
308	```
309	Adapter (frame N)          Kernel tick T                         Owner
310	  submit("begin_patch",   P1 intake: stamp issuer_peer, origin,
311	   {target}, actor,          seq, submission_id; queued_tick = T-1
312	   correlation)  ───────► P2: origin ∈ allowed_origins?
313	                              actor owned by issuer's PlayerId? ──► Interaction.validate(cmd, views, ctx)
314	                              (Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED) else)       ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason)
315	                                                                 ──► Interaction.apply(cmd, scope, ctx)
316	                                                                       Controller.set_channel_ref(...)
317	                                                                       return ctx.complete()
318	                          P3: interaction.step advances the channel each tick
319	                          P4 commit ; P5 notify (interaction.state keys)
320	  result record ◄──────── one terminal result per command (Applied / Rejected(reason) /
321	   (reason code,            Dropped / Faulted / Superseded), flushed at P5 and once per frame
322	    correlation)
323	```
324	
325	The Adapter never predicts an outcome except body motion and sound (pre-play keyed by `correlation`); light and effects change only on committed state.
326	
327	### 3. Weld transaction (cross-system atomic write)
328	
329	```
330	begin_weld (PLAYER) ── validate (static predicates only: can_join_static, socket_plan, docked)
331	   └─ apply: Interaction.open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb, target, WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS=360)
332	interaction.step × 360 ticks (re-checks lit and reach every LIT_RECHECK_TICKS)
333	assembly.step sees channel DONE ── submit_system("weld", {actor, target, cause})
334	next tick P2: weld.validate (authoritative site; full can_join) ── weld.apply, one WriteScope:
335	   Graph.weld_join (M2) → Layout.attach_section (LM2) → Body.rebase_on_attach (BM3)
336	   → Interaction.sync_section × 2 → assembly.state
337	   each call returns OK or FAULT_CODE; first non-OK → ctx.fault() → kernel FAULTED (no rollback)
338	P5: one notification batch (graph, layout, body, interaction, assembly keys) + BODY_TRANSFER
339	   → PROJECTOR rebuild, Emitter re-derives body_id (W0), Lighting rebuilds occluders, camera rebase
340	Save/Load polls Assembly.last_shape_change_T() → ASSEMBLY_WELD autosave (subject to gates)
341	```
342	
343	Cut is the same shape with M3 → LM3 → BM4; install is a TAP command (Graph `check_install_module` → M5 → Suit `release_carried` → Controller `clear_carry_ref` → `sync_section`).
344	
345	### 4. Event and notification path
346	
347	- **Simulation → presentation:** P5 notification `(block_id, tick, change_keys)` with no state payload. Dirty keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id`, namespaced per block. Past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) a batch collapses to `ALL`. PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches are merged across a multi-tick frame and delivered once; INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick.
348	- **Presentation → simulation:** only commands through an INPUT_SURFACE handle. There is no other path.
349	- **Simulation → simulation:** synchronous calls inside the tick: pure reads of another block's read view, and published mutators called inside the caller's WriteScope. A cross-block write is always a published mutator of the owning system (Class A checked or Class B clamped). Simulation code never subscribes to notifications (an object that owns a block or hook never subscribes, CR-10).
350	- **P5 events** (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`, …) are notifications that carry no simulation state; Save/Load reads them as autosave triggers.
351	- **Engine signals** are used only inside presentation (e.g. `card_opened`, settings change). The kernel's observer registry is not built on engine signals (decision for ADR-0004).
352	
353	### 5. Perception path (the one place a lie can enter)
354	
355	```
356	Sanity (SIM) ── sanity.drift ──► sanity.perception (PERCEPTION_OUT, per viewer, never persisted)
357	                                        │  (simulation reads of it return empty + violation)
358	Instrument / HUD presenter ── perceived(ref, viewer) ──► Perception Filter
359	                                        │ reads true value (Graph / Suit read view)
360	                                        │ reads sanity.perception entry for (ref, viewer)
361	                                        ▼
362	                               Perceived {displayed_value, motion_mode, leak_amplitude_pm, …}
363	Truth channels never pass through the Filter: Failure & Trail, true reveal radius (Lighting L0),
364	character sprites, crewmate beams, HUD frame, physical consequences in the Graph.
365	```
366	
367	The Graph's `state_hash` is identical with and without perception content; the simulation never computes a perceived value.
368	
369	### 6. Save path
370	
371	```
372	Trigger (interval 10 800 ticks, ASSEMBLY_WELD/CUT, SALVAGE_CUT, QUIT, NEW_GAME)
373	 └─ gates (DOWNED, refractory, suit CRITICAL, owed warning, RAGGED breach) hold or defer ≤ 7 200 ticks
374	Save/Load ── request_snapshot ──► Kernel at P6: SAVING (one boundary service, synchronous, T fixed)
375	   every persist block: snapshot(ctx) → ctx.put(plain data, deep copy, sorted ids)
376	   ◄── payloads split by persist_scope: WORLD → generation, PROFILE → profile.sav
377	Main thread: encode + hand-off ≤ SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS 4 ms
378	Worker thread (immutable PackedByteArrays + paths only):
379	   write .tmp → flush → re-read → re-hash → rotate oldest → rename → verify → campaign.json
380	   any failure: previous generations untouched, save_status FAILED, bounded backoff
381	```
382	
383	### 7. Load / restore path
384	
385	```
386	Continue / death stub ── pre-check (pure: bytes, registry view, build constants; no kernel)
387	   └─ pass: epoch staging (slot_epoch.bin write, polled per frame) → EPOCH_DURABLE
388	      (or SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE, save_status FAILED, restore proceeds — listed exposure, R14)
389	Kernel request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash) at P6: LOADING (one boundary service)
390	   restore each WORLD block in restore_after order (two-phase: decode+validate into scratch, then swap)
391	   post_restore each block in the same order (derived caches, cross-block verification)
392	   rebuild binding table half (b) from binding sources (seat_bindings, beam_bindings)
393	   reproduction check: state_hash vs header (reported, never a fallback reason)
394	   → RUNNING; accumulator cleared; camera CUT; Adapter resends intents; first frame passes through the Filter
395	```
396	
397	**restore_after order (MVP):** `layout.state` → `graph.state` → `body.state` → `controller.state` → `emitter.state`, `suit.state` → `interaction.state` → `assembly.state`, `web.state`; then Attention, Horror and Sanity (their restore_after lists are in their GDDs; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG).
398	
399	**Threading.** Exactly one thread boundary exists in the MVP: the save writer (and its read-back). Everything else, kernel, owner callables and presentation, runs on the main thread; `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden (CR-1a).

408	   invariant assertions. On any error the composition root never starts the kernel (ADR-0007 § 2.3)
409	4. Kernel BOOTING: owners register blocks, command types, hooks, binding sources, diagnostics channels
410	   (Layout, Graph last of the Item DB → Layout → Graph chain; then Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit,
411	   Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity). Registration then freezes; hook topo-sort.
412	5. Presentation subscribers subscribe (Lighting, Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, PROJECTORs, Debug)
413	6. Main menu (Chart Table) → New Game: Save/Load new_game(seed) → kernel request_new_game(seed, 0)
414	   → Web Map init_world inside one WriteScope: Layout build_section → Emitter instantiate_section_emitters
415	   → Interaction sync_section → PROJECTOR notification → initial NEW_GAME generation written

**P3 hook schedule (MVP).** Divisor and offset decide which ticks a hook runs on; `after:` orders hooks that run on the same tick. An `after:` edge between hooks that do not always run on the same tick should declare `tolerates_stale` (CR-3); an undeclared one boots with a warning (ruling R-8), so the warning list must be empty at the end of every CI run.

| Hook | Owner | Divisor | Offset | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `controller.step` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `suit.vitals` (stale-tolerant) |
| `layout.doors` | Layout | 1 | 0 | — |
| `body.integrate` | Body | 1 | 0 | `controller.step`, `layout.doors` |
| `controller.noise` | Controller | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate` |
| `emitter.place` | Emitter | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` (stale-tolerant) |
| `interaction.step` | Interaction | 1 | 0 | `emitter.place` |
| `assembly.step` | Assembly | 1 | 0 | `interaction.step` |
| `transit.step` | Web Map | 1 | 0 | `body.integrate`, `graph.propagate.failure` (**undeclared** stale edge, IC-11) |
| `graph.propagate.power` | Graph | 6 | 0 | — |
| `graph.propagate.atmo` | Graph | 6 | 2 | `graph.propagate.power` (stale-tolerant) |
| `graph.propagate.failure` | Graph | 6 | 4 | `graph.propagate.atmo` (stale-tolerant) |
| `suit.vitals` | Suit | 6 | 2 | `graph.propagate.atmo` |
| `attention.step` | Attention | 6 | 0 | `graph.propagate.power`, `emitter.place` |
| `horror.step` | Horror | 5 | 0 | `attention.step` (stale-tolerant), `emitter.place` |
| `sanity.drift` | Sanity | 12 | 0 | `graph.propagate.failure` (stale-tolerant), `suit.vitals` (stale-tolerant) |

The kernel builds this order once in BOOTING; an unknown `after:` id or a cycle fails boot. ADR-0003 records the sort; each owning GDD remains the authority on its own row.

**Budgets (P99, release export, RM-DESKTOP / RM-DECK):** P3 ≤ 2.0 ms (alarm at `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 ms); frame simulation ≤ 4.0 ms for one tick and ≤ 6.0 ms for four; Graph hooks ≤ 0.5 ms on a hook tick; `emitter.place` + exposure ≤ 0.4 ms; Sanity median ≤ 0.5 ms; pipeline `_process` ≤ 0.5 ms; light CPU ≤ 1.0 ms steady; total frame ≤ 14.9 ms desktop and ≤ 30.0 ms Deck (90 % of the 16.6 / 33.3 ms ceilings, ruling R12).

### 2. Command path (a player verb)

```
Adapter (frame N)          Kernel tick T                         Owner
  submit("begin_patch",   P1 intake: stamp issuer_peer, origin,
   {target}, actor,          seq, submission_id; queued_tick = T-1
   correlation)  ───────► P2: origin ∈ allowed_origins?
                              actor owned by issuer's PlayerId? ──► Interaction.validate(cmd, views, ctx)
                              (Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED) else)       ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason)
                                                                 ──► Interaction.apply(cmd, scope, ctx)
                                                                       Controller.set_channel_ref(...)
                                                                       return ctx.complete()
                          P3: interaction.step advances the channel each tick
                          P4 commit ; P5 notify (interaction.state keys)
  result record ◄──────── one terminal result per command (Applied / Rejected(reason) /
   (reason code,            Dropped / Faulted / Superseded), flushed at P5 and once per frame
    correlation)
```

The Adapter never predicts an outcome except body motion and sound (pre-play keyed by `correlation`); light and effects change only on committed state.

### 3. Weld transaction (cross-system atomic write)

```
begin_weld (PLAYER) ── validate (static predicates only: can_join_static, socket_plan, docked)
   └─ apply: Interaction.open_channel(seat, ASSEMBLY, verb, target, WELD_CHANNEL_TICKS=360)
interaction.step × 360 ticks (re-checks lit and reach every LIT_RECHECK_TICKS)
assembly.step sees channel DONE ── submit_system("weld", {actor, target, cause})
next tick P2: weld.validate (authoritative site; full can_join) ── weld.apply, one WriteScope:
   Graph.weld_join (M2) → Layout.attach_section (LM2) → Body.rebase_on_attach (BM3)
   → Interaction.sync_section × 2 → assembly.state
   each call returns OK or FAULT_CODE; first non-OK → ctx.fault() → kernel FAULTED (no rollback)
P5: one notification batch (graph, layout, body, interaction, assembly keys) + BODY_TRANSFER
   → PROJECTOR rebuild, Emitter re-derives body_id (W0), Lighting rebuilds occluders, camera rebase
Save/Load polls Assembly.last_shape_change_T() → ASSEMBLY_WELD autosave (subject to gates)
```

Cut is the same shape with M3 → LM3 → BM4; install is a TAP command (Graph `check_install_module` → M5 → Suit `release_carried` → Controller `clear_carry_ref` → `sync_section`).

### 4. Event and notification path

- **Simulation → presentation:** P5 notification `(block_id, tick, change_keys)` with no state payload. Dirty keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id`, namespaced per block. Past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` (256) a batch collapses to `ALL`. PRESENTATION, PROJECTOR and DIAGNOSTIC batches are merged across a multi-tick frame and delivered once; INPUT_SURFACE and REPLICATION get every tick.
- **Presentation → simulation:** only commands through an INPUT_SURFACE handle. There is no other path.
- **Simulation → simulation:** synchronous calls inside the tick: pure reads of another block's read view, and published mutators called inside the caller's WriteScope. A cross-block write is always a published mutator of the owning system (Class A checked or Class B clamped). Simulation code never subscribes to notifications (an object that owns a block or hook never subscribes, CR-10).
- **P5 events** (`BODY_TRANSFER`, `POD_ARRIVED`, `DERELICT_LOADED`, …) are notifications that carry no simulation state; Save/Load reads them as autosave triggers.
- **Engine signals** are used only inside presentation (e.g. `card_opened`, settings change). The kernel's observer registry is not built on engine signals (decision for ADR-0004).

### 5. Perception path (the one place a lie can enter)

```
Sanity (SIM) ── sanity.drift ──► sanity.perception (PERCEPTION_OUT, per viewer, never persisted)
                                        │  (simulation reads of it return empty + violation)
Instrument / HUD presenter ── perceived(ref, viewer) ──► Perception Filter
                                        │ reads true value (Graph / Suit read view)
                                        │ reads sanity.perception entry for (ref, viewer)
                                        ▼
                               Perceived {displayed_value, motion_mode, leak_amplitude_pm, …}
Truth channels never pass through the Filter: Failure & Trail, true reveal radius (Lighting L0),
character sprites, crewmate beams, HUD frame, physical consequences in the Graph.
```

The Graph's `state_hash` is identical with and without perception content; the simulation never computes a perceived value.

### 6. Save path

```
Trigger (interval 10 800 ticks, ASSEMBLY_WELD/CUT, SALVAGE_CUT, QUIT, NEW_GAME)
 └─ gates (DOWNED, refractory, suit CRITICAL, owed warning, RAGGED breach) hold or defer ≤ 7 200 ticks
Save/Load ── request_snapshot ──► Kernel at P6: SAVING (one boundary service, synchronous, T fixed)
   every persist block: snapshot(ctx) → ctx.put(plain data, deep copy, sorted ids)
   ◄── payloads split by persist_scope: WORLD → generation, PROFILE → profile.sav
Main thread: encode + hand-off ≤ SAVE_ENCODE_BUDGET_MS 4 ms
Worker thread (immutable PackedByteArrays + paths only):
   write .tmp → flush → re-read → re-hash → rotate oldest → rename → verify → campaign.json
   any failure: previous generations untouched, save_status FAILED, bounded backoff
```

### 7. Load / restore path

```
Continue / death stub ── pre-check (pure: bytes, registry view, build constants; no kernel)
   └─ pass: epoch staging (slot_epoch.bin write, polled per frame) → EPOCH_DURABLE
      (or SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE, save_status FAILED, restore proceeds — listed exposure, R14)
Kernel request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash) at P6: LOADING (one boundary service)
   restore each WORLD block in restore_after order (two-phase: decode+validate into scratch, then swap)
   post_restore each block in the same order (derived caches, cross-block verification)
   rebuild binding table half (b) from binding sources (seat_bindings, beam_bindings)
   reproduction check: state_hash vs header (reported, never a fallback reason)
   → RUNNING; accumulator cleared; camera CUT; Adapter resends intents; first frame passes through the Filter
```

**restore_after order (MVP):** `layout.state` → `graph.state` → `body.state` → `controller.state` → `emitter.state`, `suit.state` → `interaction.state` → `assembly.state`, `web.state`; then Attention, Horror and Sanity (their restore_after lists are in their GDDs; the kernel topo-sorts the declared DAG).

**Threading.** Exactly one thread boundary exists in the MVP: the save writer (and its read-back). Everything else, kernel, owner callables and presentation, runs on the main thread; `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code are lint-forbidden (CR-1a).

### 8. Initialisation order

```
1. Engine boot; project.godot guard rails asserted (stretch, filters, snap, hdr_2d, physics_interpolation off)
2. Pipeline root builds the viewport stack (BOOTING → PRESENTING)
3. Content data loads in a fixed order (ADR-0007 § 1.7): Graph type tables + GraphTuning → Item DB →
   section templates (manifest order) → world records, verb tables, tuning tables; boot lints and
   invariant assertions. On any error the composition root never starts the kernel (ADR-0007 § 2.3)
4. Kernel BOOTING: owners register blocks, command types, hooks, binding sources, diagnostics channels
   (Layout, Graph last of the Item DB → Layout → Graph chain; then Body, Controller, Emitter, Suit,
   Interaction, Assembly, Web, Attention, Horror, Sanity). Registration then freezes; hook topo-sort.
5. Presentation subscribers subscribe (Lighting, Trail, HUD, Instruments, Audio, PROJECTORs, Debug)
6. Main menu (Chart Table) → New Game: Save/Load new_game(seed) → kernel request_new_game(seed, 0)
   → Web Map init_world inside one WriteScope: Layout build_section → Emitter instantiate_section_emitters
   → Interaction sync_section → PROJECTOR notification → initial NEW_GAME generation written
   or Continue: load path (§ 7)
```

static func rng_derive(world_seed: int, stream_name: StringName, counter: int) -> int
static func rng_derive_epoch(world_seed: int, stream_name: StringName, counter: int, restore_epoch: int) -> int
```

### Perception Filter [PF-*]

```gdscript
# The only path from a true value to a corruptible display. Pull query; no block, no hook.
func perceived(ref: PerceptionRef, viewer: int) -> Perceived
# PerceptionRef kinds: GRAPH_NODE, GRAPH_COMPARTMENT, SUIT_KEY, SCANNER, HOUSING_GLOW, STATE_GLYPH, MACHINE_FRAME
```

**Guarantees:** a ref whose tag is a truth channel always returns the true value; with no active lie the result equals the true value; the Filter writes only `CanvasItem`, `Material` and `Light2D` properties and its decoy list.

### Presentation subscriber contract [PIPE PR-20, LO-1]

```gdscript
func _on_kernel_changes(batch: ChangeBatch) -> void:   # marks dirty only; no draw, no read of other blocks
	_dirty.merge(batch.change_keys)

func _process(_delta: float) -> void:                  # render callback; reads committed views at tick_alpha
	if _dirty.is_empty():
		return
	_redraw(Kernel.tick_alpha)
```

**Forbidden:** writing a block, submitting (unless INPUT_SURFACE), moving a physics body, writing the camera or a viewport property (pipeline root only), reading `sanity.perception` (Filter and Debug only).

### Save/Load host API [SL-21]

```gdscript
func new_game(world_seed: int) -> void
func save_and_quit() -> void
func continue_newest() -> void
func cancel_held_close() -> void
var save_status: SaveStatus          # IDLE, WRITING, WRITTEN, FAILED (host-local read)
```

Save/Load registers no command; `save_now` and `load(generation)` exist only in dev builds.

The signatures above use types that no GDD defines field by field. Each is defined in the named ADR before the first story that implements it; programmers must not invent them.

| Type | Defined in |
|---|---|
| `Command`, `BlockDescriptor` (full field list), `CommandTypeDescriptor`, `ReadViews`, `WriteScope`, `ApplyContext`, `SnapshotContext`, `HookContext`, `NotifyContext`, `CompletionToken` (who constructs it; per call or pooled) | ADR-0003 |
| `ChangeBatch` and the container type of `change_keys` | ADR-0004 |
| `FAULT_CODE` table: one closed enumeration per owning system, the kernel's own codes, and who may raise which | ADR-0003 |
| Per-command payload schemas and the payload validator | ADR-0002 (each command's owner lists its schema) |
| `QueryBuffer`, `SolidQuery`, `OccluderSource` | ADR-0014 |

ADR-0001 (Proposed) decides it: no autoload; the composition root hands each module the narrowest injected facet through `setup()` (presentation gets `subscribe`, read views and a read-only `PresentationClock`; submit and control rights come only from the named handles of ADR-0002). **How an interface is expressed.** GDScript has no interfaces. ADR-0010 picks one mechanism for the seams: an `@abstract` base class (4.5+, HIGH, verify; fallback a plain base class whose methods `push_error`), or duck-typed contracts checked by a boot-time registry lint.
